derivation: Sixteen orthographic views rasterized from full unreduced original authored tree meshes, sampled official photographic diffuse RGBA PNGs with their authored embedded leaf alpha preserved exactly. Two-times supersampling resolves fine true-alpha leaflets. Model-space normal RGB is relit at runtime; vector length retains unresolved normal variance. Normal-atlas alpha is a cosine-weighted hemispherical opening integrated using 64 directions through the 96³ source leaf-density volume. Color-atlas alpha is rasterized geometry coverage. Transparent borders contain nearest-covered colors and normals to avoid dark minification fringes. V5 orients each visible source normal toward its bake camera before coverage-weighted averaging. A third atlas stores coverage-weighted actual source model positions and leaf-versus-wood fraction, enabling directional crown extinction from leaf positions at runtime.

oak.sourceType: Authored geometry with photographic PBR material colors

jacaranda.sourceType: Authored geometry with photographic PBR material colors

limitations: The hemispherical aperture is a scalar. Anisotropic sky openings and multiple foliage bounces remain approximations.
Each source view captures one visible depth layer. A source point reconstructed from interpolated atlas texels can miss hidden branches and back layers.
filtering: All three atlases use joint geometry-coverage-weighted mipmaps. Mean normals retain variance, actual source positions remain in model space, and material fractions preserve mixed wood/leaf texels.
alphaDecoding: The source diffuse RGBA8 PNG alpha is used directly. Separate I;16 opacity maps are never clipped via Pillow convert(L), which would turn faint alpha into opaque white texels.

positionEncoding.rgb: Actual source model XYZ normalized within per-species sourceBounds
positionEncoding.alpha: Coverage-weighted leaf fraction, 1 for leaf material and 0 for wood
positionEncoding.purpose: Directional source-local crown sunlight extinction; geometry depth remains an impostor plane
